question: If \(x=(\log_8 2)^{(\log_2 8)},\) then \(\log_3 x\) equals:
solution:
A logarithm asks which exponent produces the stated number. Since \(8^{1/3}=2\) and \(2^3=8\),
\[
\log_8 2=\frac13,
\qquad
\log_2 8=3.
\]
Substituting these values gives
\[
x=\left(\frac13\right)^3
=\frac1{27}=3^{-3}.
\]
This value of \(x\) is positive, so its logarithm is defined. Because \(3^{-3}=x\), we obtain \(\log_3 x=\boxed{-3}\), choice A.
